commitResults.messageTitle: Correct undated lesson ordering in DG
commitResults.messageBody:

after its date is removed, but loaded histories are sorted by date.
This hides the behavior for non-oldest records and same-date ties.

Let's document the loaded ordering and exercise multiple dated,
equal-date and undated records.

The find section says ArgumentTokenizer needs an ASCII-space
boundary, but the shared tokenizer recognizes Unicode whitespace.
This contradicts the prefix-text section and the implementation.

Let's distinguish find's keyword normalization from the tokenizer's
Unicode-aware prefix recognition.

The manual test says the newly undated lesson is always last, but
existing undated records retain their relative saved order before the
view reverses them.

Let's exercise another undated record and state the ordering within the
undated group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extend find to subject and level
commitResults.messageBody:
find only searches names, so a tutor cannot bring up every student
taking one subject or at one level.

Let's accept n/, sub/ and l/ alongside bare name keywords, match every
given field with the existing all-keyword substring rule, hint at sub/
and l/ when a names-only search finds no one, and update the guides
and the brief.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat Unicode whitespace as prefix separators
commitResults.messageBody:
find only starts a field after an ASCII space, so a pasted search with
a non-breaking space or tab before l/ reads l/sec as subject keywords.

Let's turn all Unicode whitespace into plain spaces before tokenizing
in FindCommandParser, and test the prefix boundaries.

The address prefix a/ also appears in Malay and Indian names such as
Muthu a/l Raju, so add rejects them and edit silently changes the
address. The exit message also still names Address Book.

Let's use addr/ for the address, keep a/l and a/p as part of names,
hint at addr/ when add sees the old prefix, name TutorLah in the exit
message, and update the guides, brief and tests.

commitResults.messageBody:
log dates every lesson with today's date, so a lesson logged the next
day gets the wrong date. Lessons are also always added at the end, so
a later lesson for an earlier date would show as the latest in view.

Let's add an optional date/DD/MM/YYYY to log, reject impossible and
future dates, and insert each lesson in date order so that view and
deletelesson stay in step.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject signed, padded and pre-2000 lesson dates
commitResults.messageBody:
parseLessonDate accepts a signed year such as 1/1/-2026, a padded day
or month such as 001/1/2026, and typos such as 1/1/0026, because the
d/M/uuuu pattern allows signs and any number of digits.

Let's check the D/M/YYYY shape before parsing, reject dates before
01/01/2000 as likely typos, and update the UG, DG and brief to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Log rejected lesson dates and backdated inserts
commitResults.messageBody:
parseLessonDate rejects a typed date for three different reasons
with one message, and withLessonAdded can place a lesson before newer
ones, but neither leaves a trace in the log.

Let's log the reason for each rejected date, and the position of a
backdated lesson, at the fine level. Lesson content is not logged.

commitResults.messageBody:
A name made only of punctuation, such as "-", is accepted and shows
